rules.rationale: Halides showed the most negative source refractive-index effect; Moss relation inverts low polarizability into wide band gaps.
Chalcogenides raised source refractive index; polarizable S/Se/Te p-states raise valence band and shrink the gap.
Largest source effect on refractive index; covalent metalloid networks are classic narrow-gap semiconductors under the Moss inversion.
High mean-Z boosted source refractive index; diffuse heavy-atom orbitals increase bandwidth and reduce band gap.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers the dielectric source effects with reversed sign via the Moss/Ravindra inverse index-gap relation. Fails where high index and wide gap coexist, e.g. ionic heavy oxides, or where source field confidence is too low to invert reliably.

rules.rationale: Main-group halides are maximally ionic with closed-shell cations; no d-states in gap, giving the widest experimental gaps.
Strong ionicity and deep O 2p valence band place oxides high on the electronegativity-difference gap ladder.
Partially filled d bands introduce states near the Fermi level, narrowing or closing gaps; source evidence here was near-zero confidence.
Pnictides are weakly ionic covalent semiconductors; small electronegativity difference yields small experimental gaps.

skills.hypothesis: Ranks anion chemistry by cation-anion electronegativity difference and downweights the near-zero-confidence transition-metal source relation. Fails for d0 transition-metal oxides and heavily distorted or defect-dominated experimental structures where measured gaps deviate from ionicity ordering.

lesson: The source study optimized refractive index, an objective inversely coupled to band gap through the Moss relation, and its per-field confidences are low (0.006-0.30). Direct transfer would push search toward narrow-gap chalcogenides and metalloids, exactly the wrong direction. Domain ionicity chemistry supplies the same ordering with independent mechanistic support, so it is the safer frozen deployment while the inverted-transfer skill remains the diagnostic alternative.
